newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods, led by heat, soar like eagles.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods, led by heat, soar like eagles.

text.p: U.S. spot heating oil continued to defy gravity late Thursday by soaring 2.75 cents a gallon with NYMEX futures, helping tug gasoline sharply higher, traders said.

Heat was lifted in part by the onset of cooler weather in the Northeast that made traders mindful of a worrisome statistic -- heating oil stocks in the region stand 19 million barrels below this time last year.
New York Harbor heat was offered at a half cent over November futures, stable with Wednesday, as Gulf diffs firmed about 0.10 cent to 2.15 cents below the print, traders said.
But distillate activity was thin, one Gulf trader said, as the market balked at seasonally stratospheric prices hovering 20 cents a gallon above 1995 levels.
"These are dangerously high numbers. People don't want to buy and are afraid to sell," one Gulf trader said. "You can get in, but you might not be able to get out."
Forecasts for the Northeast, the largest U.S. heating oil market, call for temperatures 8-16 degrees Fahrenheit below normal Friday and slightly below normal by Sunday.
